enonce_intro_markdown:
Two statements are such that

$p$: Peter is studying English Language

$q$: Peter will live in Britain
incertitudes: Le sujet imprime « P: peter is studying English Language » avec un P majuscule dans la premiere declaration ; transcrit en $p$ car la suite du sujet utilise $p \to q$.

questions.corrige_markdown:
$p \to q$ reads "if $p$ then $q$":

**If Peter is studying English Language, then Peter will live in Britain.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the notation and translate in ordinary English the converse of $p \to q$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The converse swaps the two statements: notation $q \to p$.

**If Peter will live in Britain, then Peter is studying English Language.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the notation and translate in ordinary English the inverse of $p \to q$. *[6 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The inverse negates both statements: notation $\sim p \to \sim q$ (also written $\neg p \to \neg q$).

**If Peter is not studying English Language, then Peter will not live in Britain.**
